tasks.short: Search files and contact parties for the court.

steps.what: Search files for the names the court listed.
Write down the information they provided.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store searches files for the names the court listed and shows the hits. The registry clerk contacts the witness, attorney, or litigant and writes down the information they provided. The search does not decide whom to call beyond that list, and it does not call anyone. An ambiguous name is not opened. No recording of the call is added.
tasks.previous_blocker: The clerk searched paper and then called, often the wrong file because two people shared a name.
tasks.enabler_now: A name the court has listed can find a file. The call is still the clerk.
tasks.still_hard: People do not answer, names collide, and what they say may not be what the court hoped.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk can tell a reluctant witness from a wrong number, and can stop when the person should not be pressed.
tasks.altitude: The right file is more often open before the call. Contacting people and writing what they said stay with the clerk. The week is still mostly the phone.

reach.task: Stay on the call and record what the person actually said.
reach.learn: A file can be found by a listed name. The call stays a person, as it does for a telecommunicator.

evidence.claim: A file store can search names the court listed. It cannot conduct the call.

The job digest says a machine that speaks to the public must identify itself, and call recording needs works-council consent. This clerk makes the call. Nothing is recorded by a new system. The note is not a witness statement taken under oath.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: The desk is a European municipal court registry and licensing counter. The sentence uses US public-sector wording and is read as the local court, council, or permit this municipality actually issues.

Fields: The name list is produced by the court, with a role for each name (witness, attorney, or litigant). Two files for one name stop the search and the clerk chooses. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the clerk finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the existing case file search before a new index.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the clerk.
unknowns: Whether the court provides a stable person id or only a name.
Which contacts the clerk is allowed to make without the judge.
research_questions: How often does a name match two files?
Are calls already recorded under a works-council agreement?

already_counted.description: The clerk still makes the contact.
The clerk still writes what was said.

incremental.description: The clerk adds a name-match note when two files collide.

approvals.approved_version: name, file id, and the note text shown to the clerk

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The calls are the task. Saving is the file search, and it shrinks when names are ambiguous and the clerk still hunts the right file before dialling.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The clerk still contacts witnesses, attorneys, and litigants. A file search by the names the court listed is the only part that leaves the hour.
reach: Library assistants search a catalogue for a name and then fetch the item by hand.
Public safety telecommunicators stay on the call until the person has given the fact, and this desk learns the contact cannot be a script.
skills_to_grow: Search only the names the court listed, and stop when the name is ambiguous.
Write what the person said, and not what the file suggests they meant.
role.ambitious_version: The named file is open before the clerk dials, and the call itself is still the clerk.
